**Date:** April 2020  
**Type:** Recorded guest lecture (Michigan State University)  
**Host:** Dr. William E. McCarthy, MSU  
**Presenter:** Kip Twitchell  
**Also present:** Rick Roth, Eric Denna, Rakesh Conte

## Context

Kip Twitchell delivered a guest lecture to Dr. William E. McCarthy's graduate students at Michigan State University in April 2020. Dr. McCarthy originated the **Resource, Event, and Agent (REA)** economic accounting model. Eric Denna (Kip's academic mentor, PhD from MSU) made the introduction; Rick Roth (Kip's boss for 19 years at Price Waterhouse) and Rakesh Conte (collaborator) joined the call.

Kip framed the lecture as his "30-year report" on what he built on the foundations of REA and the SAFR (Structured Architecture for Financial Reporting) work from the Price Waterhouse practice led by Rick Roth.

The lecture covers:
- The daily financial cycle: transactions vs. balances and the data growth trade-off
- The **Minimum Cost Curve** — an isoquant chart showing the optimal mix of transactions and balances for producing a body of analytical outputs at minimum cost (five years in development, published on ledgerlearning.com)
- Historical computing cost curves (1964 to present) as the structural cause of high-level aggregated ledger architectures
- Why sub-ledger consistency and just-in-time analytics are the path forward
- Q&A covering healthcare data volumes, blockchain implications, and the role of detailed event capture

The deck (40 slides) and this transcript are the historical starting point for the Sharealedger conceptual model. The deck was created with IBM authorization and contributed to Sharealedger; original slide attributions and notices remain in the deck.
